Predictions, even by the best of experts, are really just educated guesses. An economist might tell me that he predicts that China's GDP growth will slow down to 1.5% in the next year based on a variety of economic laws and data. His calculations might be entirely correct, and China's GDP may actually not conform to his predictions.

However, that doesn't mean I should not trust the economist - the theories he uses are fundamentally sound, and the reason his prediction is off the mark, is that the real world has so much data that there is no way that anyone can make accurate predictions regarding anything, by more than just pure luck.

It's the same with the media. They'll make predictions about who will win, and so on - and the information that they base their guesses on might be correct - but at the same time, even if their information is correct, there's so much information that even they don't know. This, however, does not mean I'll distrust the information they report - just the predictions. Not that I ever put much stock in predictions anyway.
